title: Try a new case
subtitle: An optional written transfer check after the ten chapters
intro: Try this fictional case without your notes. Allow twenty to thirty minutes. Write somewhere private; this page does not collect or grade your answers. Compare with the suggested reasoning after your attempt.
paragraphs: A musician values performing but misses rehearsals that conflict with care work. Another cares about the concert but doubts the current practice strategy. The conductor calls both unmotivated.
A new plan offers complete freedom but no guidance. A quota rewards speed over accurate playing. A member wants a solo and fears public criticism at the same time.

Before a performance, a pulse increase and a smile are treated as proof of happiness. Members are told to suppress all concern, including concerns about an unsafe stage. Different visible apologies after mistakes are ranked as moral character.
A workshop promises permanent motivation after participants report feeling better immediately. There is no comparison or later measure.

tasks.title: Goals, constraints and value
tasks.prompt: Distinguish value, expectancy, bodily needs, incentives and opportunity in the rehearsal choices.
tasks.answer: Absence can reflect caring constraints rather than low value. Valuing a concert differs from expecting a strategy to work. Bodily states and situational incentives can contribute without uniquely explaining the action. Ask respectfully and compare feasible routes.

tasks.title: Support and goals
tasks.prompt: Revise the freedom-only plan and speed quota.
tasks.answer: Provide meaningful choice, clear guidance, useful feedback and connection. Use learning and process goals when needed, and measure musical accuracy and safety rather than count alone. Revise a goal if its proxy creates harm.

tasks.title: Conflict and emotion
tasks.prompt: Explain the solo conflict and limits of the pulse and smile claims.
tasks.answer: Approach to a valued outcome can coexist with avoidance of criticism. Pulse and expression are components whose meaning needs context and self-report. They do not uniquely identify happiness or any other emotion.

tasks.title: Regulation and social meaning
tasks.prompt: Respond to the unsafe stage and different apologies.
tasks.answer: Address the hazard instead of requiring positive reinterpretation or suppression. Expression norms and individual feelings vary; assess actual repair actions and ask what support is wanted rather than ranking visible emotion.

tasks.title: Evaluate the workshop
tasks.prompt: Propose a credible test and a bounded recommendation.
tasks.answer: Define a meaningful outcome, use a credible comparison and delayed follow-up, assess quality and unwanted effects, and preserve voluntary participation. Immediate mood is not durable efficacy. Persistent distress may need professional support rather than motivational pressure.

rubric.title: Accurate distinctions
rubric.strong: Explains the relevant concepts and separates observations from interpretations.
rubric.developing: Adds labels without explaining how the evidence supports them.

rubric.title: Evidence and alternatives
rubric.strong: Considers competing explanations and a comparison that could distinguish them.
rubric.developing: Treats a plausible account, score or correlation as a settled cause.

rubric.title: Proportionate application
rubric.strong: States limitations, respects the people involved and explains what would change the recommendation.
rubric.developing: Overgeneralizes to individuals or makes a recommendation beyond the evidence.

followup: Return tomorrow or in a week with an unfamiliar example. Compare the quality of your explanation, not just your confidence. This self-check does not certify professional competence or establish general mastery.
